sense: someone who does it for a living, not as an amateur

terms.gloss: a professional, a master of an art
terms.comment: The practitioner as against the layman, idiōta (Cic. Verr. 2.4.4: quōs iste idiōtās appellat); artificēs scaenicī are professional performers (Cic. Arch. 10, Lewis & Short). For “professional” meaning “to do with one’s work”, Latin uses the noun: ars, artificium.

evidence: Cic. Imp. Pomp. 68: bellōrum omnium perītissimus (Lewis & Short)

phrases.latin: Ut ajunt in Graecīs artificibus eōs auloedōs esse quī citharoedī fierī nōn potuerint
phrases.english: As they say of Greek professional musicians, that those who could not become lyre-singers become pipe-singers

sources: Lewis & Short: artifex · Lewis & Short: idiota · Lewis & Short: peritus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. professional photographer; expert.
